import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/titanic.csv')

# Set the aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", context="talk")

# Create a figure and axes for the plot
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 8))

# Create the bar plot using seaborn
# This plot shows the survival rate broken down by passenger class and 'who' (man, woman, child)
# Seaborn's barplot automatically calculates the mean of 'survived' for each category, which is the survival rate.
g = sns.barplot(
    data=df,
    x='class',
    y='survived',
    hue='who',
    order=['First', 'Second', 'Third'],
    hue_order=['woman', 'child', 'man'],
    palette={'woman': '#4e79a7', 'child': '#f28e2b', 'man': '#e15759'},
    ax=ax,
    ci=None # Disable confidence intervals for clarity
)

# --- Add annotations and labels for clarity ---

# Add percentage labels on top of each bar
for p in ax.patches:
    height = p.get_height()
    if height > 0:
        ax.annotate(f'{height:.0%}',
                    (p.get_x() + p.get_width() / 2., height),
                    ha='center',
                    va='center',
                    xytext=(0, 9),
                    textcoords='offset points',
                    fontsize=12,
                    color='black')

# Set plot title and labels
ax.set_title('Survival Rate on the Titanic by Class and Category', fontsize=20, pad=20, weight='bold')
ax.set_xlabel('Passenger Class', fontsize=14, labelpad=15)
ax.set_ylabel('Survival Rate', fontsize=14, labelpad=15)

# Format the y-axis to show percentages
ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(mticker.PercentFormatter(xmax=1.0))
ax.set_ylim(0, 1.05) # Give some space for the annotations above the bars

# Customize the legend
handles, labels = ax.get_legend_handles_labels()
ax.legend(handles, ['Woman', 'Child', 'Man'], title='Category', title_fontsize='13', fontsize='12', frameon=True)

# Add a descriptive subtitle
fig.text(0.5, 0.92,
         'Survival chances were highest for women and children, especially in First and Second Class.',
         ha='center', va='center', fontsize=14, style='italic', color='dimgray')

# Improve layout
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 1, 0.95]) # Adjust layout to make room for suptitle

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

# Close the plot to free up memory
plt.close(fig)
